Every acceptance criterion of t4 is checked against raw output the verifier produced; anything unreproducible is reported as a failure, not waved through

the vendor-refresh guard exercised with its anchor removed

view.reassign_reason:
RETRY after repair t13 landed. All three findings you raised are claimed closed; I verified the substance myself before writing this, so you know what to re-derive rather than what to trust:
- `bun test packages` = 340 pass / 0 fail.
- F2: `lib/mpd-deltas.js` now registers 9 regions, including the three groups you named as unmarked (scope-overlap, scope-overlap-normalize, create-contract-gate); `pathMatchesScope` is wholly inside scope-glob so a re-materialize cannot strand an upstream copy.
- F1: the carve-out is real — `quality-gates.js:347-348`: `const carved = sourceOutOfScope.filter((pattern) => !required.some((file) => pathMatchesScope(file, pattern)))` returned as the new outOfScope alongside `allowed` in inScope.
- F3: the heal path now refuses when a module-scope name it declares still exists outside every region, plus post-heal validation, and `vendor-agent-teams.mjs` turns the refusal into exit 1.

TWO OF YOUR OWN DRIVERS HAVE STALE EXPECTATIONS NOW — do not read them as regressions:
1. `check4-guard` hard-codes "7 regions" (the registry is 9 now), and its S5 mutates the `scope-glob-core` region, which no longer exists as a separate region (it was merged into `scope-glob`). So S5's mutation silently no-ops and S1 prints 9. The in-region drift case S5 is trying to exercise IS verified, just not by that path: mutating one line inside `scope-glob` makes `--check` exit 1 naming the exact line ("lines 102-195 … first difference at line 118") while the pristine tree exits 0. Update those two constants in your drivers and re-run, rather than reporting S5's `exit=0 … want 1` as a failure.
2. `check5-mount`'s `passed:false` is its WORKSPACE-ISOLATION counter, not the mount. The flagged `.mpd/team/mpd-default-587132ea` was created at 14:19:47 by captain session `session-8954c880-eee` — a CONCURRENT session, not this boot. That boot's own leak counter is 0 (`real_workspace_session_keys_in_sandbox=0`) and it reports 14/14 tools with 0 apply-crash signatures. Before calling any flagged record a leak, check the creating session id.
   Mechanism worth recording: the SESSION-START TEAM POLICY auto-provisions a team for every new session in this workspace, so concurrent members' sessions legitimately create `mpd-default-*` records in `<repo>/.mpd/team`. That is expected behavior and NOT t7's isolation failing — it is why the repo accumulates these records, and it is why that counter is noisy while other sessions run.

WHAT TO DO: re-run your FULL t8 contract against the current tree — the tree moved (quality-gates.js, mpd-deltas.js, the self-fix test, both scripts), so treat your attempt-1 pass list as requiring re-confirmation rather than transferable. Specifically re-check the three findings against the REAL archived inputs (F1's success signal: the finding's file is `in_scope` while prohibitions NO finding requires — VENDOR_LOCK.json, presets/mpd/agent.cordis.yml — still hold; that preserved-prohibition side is the falsifiability control, so verify it did not get over-carved), the region coverage (no executable added line outside a region), and the F3 refusal (non-zero exit naming the symbol and line, refused file byte-identical to its input, clean re-materialize still heals byte-identically).
If everything holds, complete t8 as a pass; t10 has been waiting on it since attempt 1.
